sections.title: From Concrete to Abstract (0:00-1:00)
lecture_lines: Vectors are more than just geometric arrows.
Consider vectors as abstract objects in sets.
These sets follow specific rules of engagement.
Linearity defines the structure of vector spaces.
animations: Fade in a 2D vector arrow originating from the origin. (Color: #FFFFFF)

sections.title: The Eight Axioms: The Rules of the Game (1:00-2:30)
lecture_lines: Vector spaces require two fundamental operations.
Addition and scalar multiplication structure our space.
These operations must satisfy eight core axioms.
Polynomials follow these same algebraic rules.
Different structures obey identical structural laws.
animations: Display all 8 axioms as text on the screen. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Animate group by group, highlighting each with a subtle glow. (Color: #FF8080)
Show a visual example of the additive inverse axiom. (Color: #80FF80)

sections.title: Beyond Arrows: Diverse Vector Spaces (2:30-4:00)
lecture_lines: Vector spaces are surprisingly diverse structures.
Functions act as vectors in function spaces.
Adding functions mirrors geometric vector addition.
animations: Display a function graph next to a standard coordinate vector [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg]. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Highlight the common structural properties between them [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg]. (Color: #FF8080)
Morph the arrow vector into the function curve [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg]. (Color: #80FF80)

sections.title: The Power of Abstraction (4:00-5:00)
lecture_lines: Abstraction provides a unified mathematical framework.
Properties proven once apply to all spaces.
Diverse systems share the same underlying logic.
